description: Stateless liveness/readiness probe: no database, dependencies, or external calls. Use it to verify reachability and read the running service/API versions.
Returns the largest value in the dataset. Accepts 1–10,000 finite numbers.
Returns the arithmetic mean of `values` (Σ xᵢ / n). Uses Neumaier compensated summation, so datasets with widely varying magnitudes keep low-order digits. Accepts 1–10,000 finite numbers.
Returns the middle value of the sorted dataset, or the mean of the two middle values when the count is even. Accepts 1–10,000 finite numbers.
Returns the smallest value in the dataset. Accepts 1–10,000 finite numbers.

Returns the `percentile`-th percentile of `values` using linear interpolation between closest ranks (the NumPy/`PERCENTILE` inclusive definition). `percentile` is a finite number in [0, 100]; 0 is the minimum and 100 is the maximum. Accepts 1–10,000 finite numbers.
Returns `max − min`, the spread of the dataset. Non-negative by construction. Accepts 1–10,000 finite numbers.
Returns the population standard deviation σ, the square root of the population variance (divided by n). Non-negative; accepts 1–10,000 finite numbers.
Returns the sum of `values` (Σ xᵢ), decimal-exact. Equivalent to `/api/v1/math/add` for numeric arrays. Accepts 1–10,000 finite numbers.
Returns the population variance σ² = (Σ (xᵢ − μ)²) / n (divided by n, not n−1). Decimal-exact two-pass computation. Non-negative; accepts 1–10,000 finite numbers.
Returns the sum of `values` (Σ valuesᵢ). Decimal-exact internally (40 significant digits), so `[0.1, 0.2]` returns `0.3`. Accepts 1–10,000 finite numbers; negatives and zero are allowed.

Returns the number of unordered selections `C(n, r) = n! / (r! (n − r)!)`. `n` and `r` are integers from 0 to 1,000 and the contract requires `r ≤ n`. Exact integer results beyond `Number.MAX_SAFE_INTEGER` are returned as decimal strings and are never rounded.
Returns `values₀ ÷ values₁ ÷ values₂ ÷ …`, evaluated strictly left to right. Requires at least 2 finite values. A zero divisor is a `DIVISION_BY_ZERO` domain error (HTTP 422), not a validation error.
Returns `n!` for an integer n from 0 to 1,000 (`0! = 1`). Exact integer results beyond `Number.MAX_SAFE_INTEGER` are returned as decimal strings and are never rounded.
Returns the greatest common divisor of two integers, sign-independently. `gcd(0, b) = |b|`; `gcd(0, 0)` yields `UNDEFINED_RESULT` (HTTP 422). Both inputs must be safe integers.
Returns the least common multiple of two integers, sign-independently. `lcm(0, b) = 0`; `lcm(0, 0)` yields `UNDEFINED_RESULT` (HTTP 422). Both inputs must be safe integers.
Returns the natural logarithm (base e). `value ≤ 0` yields `UNDEFINED_RESULT` (HTTP 422).
Returns the logarithm of `value` to `base`. `base` is optional and defaults to 10. `value ≤ 0`, `base ≤ 0`, and `base = 1` yield `UNDEFINED_RESULT` (HTTP 422).
Returns the product of `values` (Π valuesᵢ). Decimal-exact internally. Accepts 1–10,000 finite numbers.

Returns the principal real `degree`-th root of `value`. `degree` is an integer from 1 to 10,000. An even root of a negative value yields `UNDEFINED_RESULT` (422); odd roots of negatives return the negative real root.
Returns `(percentage / 100) × value`. Both inputs are finite numbers (negatives allowed).

Returns `((to − from) / from) × 100` as percent points (so `25` means +25%). The signed `from` value is the denominator. `from = 0` has no defined relative change and yields `DIVISION_BY_ZERO` (HTTP 422).

Returns the number of ordered selections `P(n, r) = n! / (n − r)!`. `n` and `r` are integers from 0 to 1,000 and the contract requires `r ≤ n`. Exact integer results beyond `Number.MAX_SAFE_INTEGER` are returned as decimal strings and are never rounded.

summary: Raise a base to an exponent
description: Returns `base^exponent`. `0^0 = 1` and `0^positive = 0` by convention; `0^negative` yields `DIVISION_BY_ZERO` (422); a negative base with a non-integer exponent yields `UNDEFINED_RESULT` (422); overflow/underflow yield `UNDEFINED_RESULT` (422).
Returns the principal (non-negative) square root. A negative input has no real square root and yields `UNDEFINED_RESULT` (HTTP 422).
Returns `values₀ − values₁ − values₂ − …`, evaluated strictly left to right (the array is the expression). Requires at least two finite values.
Returns `revenue / orders`. `revenue` is signed; `orders` is non-negative. `orders = 0` yields `DIVISION_BY_ZERO` (HTTP 422).

Returns `fixedCosts / (price − variableCost)`, the number of units needed to cover fixed costs (may be fractional). A contribution of `price − variableCost ≤ 0` makes break-even unreachable and yields `UNDEFINED_RESULT` (HTTP 422).
Returns `cost / customers`. `customers = 0` yields `DIVISION_BY_ZERO` (HTTP 422).

Returns `((endValue / beginValue)^(1 / periods) − 1) × 100` as percent points. `periods` must be greater than 0. `beginValue ≤ 0` or `endValue < 0` yields `UNDEFINED_RESULT` (HTTP 422); overflow yields `UNDEFINED_RESULT`; a total loss returns `−100`.
Returns `churned / starting × 100` as percent points. Counts are non-negative. `starting = 0` yields `DIVISION_BY_ZERO` (HTTP 422).

Returns `averageOrderValue × purchasesPerPeriod × lifespanPeriods`. No currency is assumed. Exact integer results beyond `Number.MAX_SAFE_INTEGER` are returned as decimal strings and are never rounded.
Returns `conversions / sessions × 100` as percent points. Counts are non-negative. `sessions = 0` yields `DIVISION_BY_ZERO` (HTTP 422).
Returns `cost / conversions`. `conversions = 0` yields `DIVISION_BY_ZERO` (HTTP 422).
Returns `cost / clicks`. `cost` and `clicks` are non-negative. `clicks = 0` yields `DIVISION_BY_ZERO` (HTTP 422).
Returns `cost / impressions × 1000` (cost per 1,000 impressions). `impressions = 0` yields `DIVISION_BY_ZERO` (HTTP 422).
Returns `clicks / impressions × 100` as percent points. Counts are non-negative. `impressions = 0` yields `DIVISION_BY_ZERO` (HTTP 422).
Returns `(price − cost) / cost × 100` as percent points. `cost = 0` yields `DIVISION_BY_ZERO` (HTTP 422). Distinct from margin, which is based on revenue/price.
Returns `revenue − costs`. Monetary inputs are signed (negative results are meaningful losses).
Returns `(revenue − costs) / revenue × 100` as percent points (`40` means 40%). `revenue = 0` yields `DIVISION_BY_ZERO` (HTTP 422).
Returns `retained / starting × 100` as percent points. Counts are non-negative. `starting = 0` yields `DIVISION_BY_ZERO` (HTTP 422).
Returns `revenue / adSpend` as a plain ratio (`4` means 4×). `adSpend = 0` yields `DIVISION_BY_ZERO` (HTTP 422). Unlike ROI, this is not multiplied by 100.
Returns `profit / investment × 100` as percent points, where `profit` is the net gain. `investment = 0` yields `DIVISION_BY_ZERO` (HTTP 422). Distinct from ROAS, which is a revenue ratio.
